svg.title: RTMSF deployment architecture on Azure
svg.desc: Planned Azure architecture: ADLS Gen2 emits committed file creation and deletion events through Event Grid into a Service Bus queue. One Azure VM systemd worker runs the existing routing, WOERA, and PMCP core through Azure adapters. It renews PeekLock deliveries, completes reconciled input, and uses native Service Bus dead-letter settlement for terminal input. PMCP reads authoritative storage and manages explicit external Parquet partition metadata through a Databricks SQL warehouse and Unity Catalog. Azure managed identity authorizes queue and storage access; Databricks OAuth machine-to-machine authorizes SQL access. The Unity Catalog access connector authorizes query reads from storage. Azure VM Run Command installs source and dependencies in Azure; the VM journal records proof logs. The OAuth secret is entered into Azure Key Vault by the user. The VM and Key Vault are deployed, and the SQL catalog proof and decoder unit tests have passed. The event pipeline, unattended authentication, and worker runtime remain unverified. Microsoft Azure service icons retain their official shapes and colors; Run Command and VM journal use generic symbols.
svg.text: VM deployed · Catalog proof and decoder tests passed · Event pipeline pending
One systemd worker · no public IP or inbound ports
Resolve existing tables and match exact object paths
Group partition observations within Q / T_max
Verify storage and reconcile catalog membership
Python core reused · Azure adapters · bounded calls
Primary storage HEAD / bounded paginated LIST
Current evidence: catalog SQL + 107 Azure unit tests. Azure event delivery, cloud worker, OAuth login, and recovery remain unverified.
Official Microsoft Azure icons · Solid: runtime calls · Dashed: support · Worker and proof execution belong in Azure.
